prompt:
Architectural floor plan of one room, drawn straight from above as a clean top-down orthographic plan view in the style of a set designer's ground plan: white background, thick dark walls with gaps for doors and windows, door swings drawn as arcs, windows as thin double lines, and every piece of furniture as a simple outline from above, to scale. In the plan, its bottom edge is the front wall, its top edge the back wall, its left edge the left wall and its right edge the right wall, as the establishing view names them. Draw only the doors, windows and openings the description names. Location: Jail, front desk. A present-day jail processing and release area with beige walls and a grey linoleum floor. A chest-high grey laminate front desk runs across the room, parallel to the back wall and a few steps in front of it, with a computer monitor and a tray on its top. Back wall: grey metal filing cabinets, a plain round wall clock and, at the back wall's left end, a heavy steel security door with a small wire-glass pane, which leads back to the cells. Right wall: a heavy steel exit door with a push bar and a small wire-glass window, the way out to the street. Left wall: a row of small grey steel property lockers and a steel bench bolted to the floor beneath them. Front wall (behind the camera): a cork notice board. Rectangular fluorescent ceiling panels give cool, even top light, and daylight comes in faintly through the exit door's small window on the right wall.

Avoid: people, text, labels, numbers, letters, dimensions, compass, logos, watermark, a door or window the description does not name.
